memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not make idols or set up an image or a sacred stone for
yourselves, and do not place a carved stone in your land to bow down
before it. I am the LORD your God'" - Lev 26:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As this great chapter of blessing and warning begins, God returns to the
very first thing: worship Him alone. Before He speaks of harvests or
hardship, He addresses the heart's deepest tendency — to put something in
His place.

Notice how many forms He lists: idols, images, sacred stones, carved
stones. He is closing every loophole. The human heart is endlessly
creative in finding substitutes for God.

Dear friend, we may not carve stones today, but the temptation is
identical. An idol is simply anything we look to for what only God can
give — security, identity, comfort, meaning. It can be money, a career, a
relationship, an image of ourselves, even a ministry.

The trouble with idols is that they always disappoint. The prophet said
those who make idols become like them — lifeless and unable to help (Ps
115:8). Idols promise much and deliver nothing.

Jesus said no one can serve two masters (Matt 6:24). John ends his
letter with a plain command: dear children, keep yourselves from idols
(1 John 5:21).

The safeguard against idolatry is not merely resisting false gods; it is
being captivated by the true one. When God is genuinely first, the
substitutes lose their grip.

What have you been quietly looking to instead of God? Bring it into the
light today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I looking to for what only God can give?
2. Where has something good drifted into God's rightful place?
3. What would it look like to make God genuinely first this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You alone are God, and nothing else deserves the place that
belongs to You. Show me my idols, and capture my heart afresh with
Yourself. Amen.
